issues.description: The problem statement and client controller expect REST endpoints under the path /persons (e.g. POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{id}, DELETE /persons/{id}) but the solution server implementation exposes these endpoints under /people. This creates a structural mismatch between client and server (and between the template specification and the provided solution) that will prevent the client and server from communicating and confuses students about the intended endpoint naming.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the server endpoints use the /persons path to match the problem statement and client (or, if /people is preferred, update the problem statement and client controller to use /people). Concretely, change the @GetMapping/@PostMapping/@PutMapping/@DeleteMapping annotations in src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java to use "persons" instead of "people", or update client URI usages to the same path to ensure both sides agree.

issues.description: The problem statement and the client-side controller use the resource path '/persons' for the Person CRUD endpoints, but the server-side implementation in the solution exposes the endpoints under '/people'. This naming mismatch (persons vs. people) creates a clear mapping confusion: client requests to /persons will not reach the server's /people endpoints and the problem description asks for /persons. Students will be unable to reconcile requirements, client code, and server implementation without resolving this naming divergence.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the server resource paths consistent with the problem statement and client by renaming the mappings in PersonResource from 'people' to 'persons' (e.g., @GetMapping("persons"), @PostMapping("persons"), @PutMapping("persons/{personId}"), @DeleteMapping("persons/{personId}")). Alternatively, change client URIs to use '/people' and update the problem statement, but prefer aligning the server to '/persons' to match the exercise description and client code.
